summary: This document outlines the requirements for building a full-stack web application that tracks contacts while ensuring strict data privacy. The project requires implementing user authentication, database persistence, and Row Level Security to prevent unauthorized access between users.
key_facts: Build a public web application deployed on Vercel
Sign-in and sign-out flow using Neon Managed Better Auth
A private contact list for each authenticated user
Create, view, edit, delete, sort, and filter contact records
Priority accepts only high, medium, or low
The contacts table includes a text user_id that defaults to auth.user_id() and cannot be null
Row Level Security is enabled on the contacts table

concepts.name: Neon Postgres
concepts.in_this_source: The project requires using Neon Postgres for persistent data storage.

concepts.name: Managed Better Auth
concepts.definition: An authentication service for managing user sessions and sign-in flows.
concepts.in_this_source: The project requires implementing a sign-in and sign-out flow using Managed Better Auth.

concepts.name: Row Level Security
concepts.definition: A security mechanism that restricts database access to specific rows based on user identity.
concepts.in_this_source: The project requires enabling Row Level Security on the contacts table to ensure users can only access their own data.

concepts.name: Vercel
concepts.definition: A cloud platform for hosting and deploying web applications.
concepts.in_this_source: The project requires deploying the final web application on Vercel.

concepts.name: Neon Data API
concepts.definition: Neon's PostgREST-based HTTP interface to a Postgres database, called with the end user's own JWT.
concepts.in_this_source: A required part of the stack; the frontend may use its public URL, so RLS must protect every exposed contacts row.
